intro.text: This entry describes brain small vessel disease-4 (BSVD4), one of a genetically heterogeneous group of hereditary cerebral small vessel diseases.

checks.claim: Brain small vessel disease-4 (BSVD4) is one of a genetically heterogeneous group of hereditary cerebral small vessel diseases.
checks.evidence_quote: NIT1-small vessel disease is a novel, autosomal recessively inherited cerebral small vessel disease characterized by a triad of movement disorders, massively dilated basal ganglia perivascular spaces, and intracerebral hemorrhage.
checks.explanation: The abstract presents NIT1-SVD as a novel hereditary cerebral small vessel disease. It does not use the designation BSVD4 or call the group genetically heterogeneous.

paragraphs.text: Brain small vessel disease refers to hereditary disorders that affect the small arteries, arterioles, capillaries and venules of the brain. They typically cause white matter abnormalities (leukoencephalopathy), lacunar infarcts, microbleeds and/or intracerebral hemorrhage. Clinically, they may present with stroke, cognitive decline or other neurologic deficits.

checks.claim: Brain small vessel disease refers to hereditary disorders that affect the small arteries, arterioles, capillaries and venules of the brain.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not define brain small vessel disease or discuss small arteries, arterioles, capillaries or venules.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases typically cause white matter abnormalities (leukoencephalopathy).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not say what hereditary small vessel diseases typically cause. It mentions white matter only in the context of 'vanishing white matter diseases.'

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases typically cause lacunar infarcts.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not say that hereditary small vessel diseases cause lacunar infarcts. It mentions only 'cerebral porosis' in a historical classification of lacunar lesions.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases typically cause microbleeds.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not mention microbleeds.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases typically cause intracerebral hemorrhage.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not mention intracerebral hemorrhage.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases may present clinically with stroke.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper says only that a stroke was suspected in its own index patient. It makes no general statement about how hereditary small vessel diseases present.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases may present clinically with cognitive decline.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper describes neuropsychological deterioration in its own patients but says nothing about small vessel diseases in general.

checks.claim: Hereditary brain small vessel diseases may present clinically with other neurologic deficits.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper makes no general statement about how hereditary small vessel diseases present clinically.

paragraphs.text: Brain small vessel disease is genetically heterogeneous. BSVD1 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the COL4A1 gene on chromosome 13q34. BSVD2 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the COL4A2 gene on chromosome 13q34. BSVD3 is caused by biallelic mutation in the COLGALT1 gene.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not discuss genetic heterogeneity of brain small vessel disease.
